end.summary:
Practised identifying east from sunrise and using a magnet to find north-south.
Reviewed keeping a compass needle flat and observing its direction.
Practised that a freely suspended magnet’s north pole points roughly north.
Introduced the Earth as a giant magnet; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Mahi practised finding directions with a magnet and explaining why a simple compass works. They correctly stated that a freely suspended magnet settles north-south and noted that it should be kept flat. They were unsure about why the needle points north and mixed up the role of the Earth’s magnetic poles; this was not confirmed corrected by the end. At home, use a magnetised needle floating on a small piece of cork and ask Mahi to observe its direction, then explain that Earth behaves like a giant magnet.
